slides.heading: Shift Linked List
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Shift Linked List, a hard linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Rotate the list k positions forward (k > 0) or backward (k < 0); return the new head.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Rotate the list k positions forward (k over 0) or backward (k under 0); return the new head.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Rotation is just choosing a new tail: connect the old tail to the head and cut at length minus k.
slides.narration: Rotation is just choosing a new tail: connect the old tail to the head and cut at length minus k.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Shift one node at a time k times → O(n·k)
slides.narration: Rotating one step at a time is n times k. Computing the length and cutting once is linear.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 4. Rewire and return the new head
slides.narration: Step by step. First, find length and tail. Second, normalise k modulo length. Third, walk to the new tail. Fourth, rewire and return the new head.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Length 6; shift 2 → effective 2
slides.narration: Find the length, 6, and the tail. Shifting by 2 is the same as 2 modulo the length.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: New tail at index 3
slides.narration: The new tail is 3 steps from the start: node 3. Its next, 4, becomes the new head.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Cut and reconnect
slides.narration: Cut after the new tail and connect the old tail to the old head.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We walk to the tail counting length, compute the effective shift, walk to the new tail, cut, link the old tail to the old head, and return the new head.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Take k mod length, using floor mod so negative k works.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Rotation is just choosing a new tail: connect the old tail to the head and cut at length minus k.
slides.narration: To recap Shift Linked List: Rotation is just choosing a new tail: connect the old tail to the head and cut at length minus k. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
